input: This passage presents the results of a duty assessment for a centrifugal pump that is used to move water between two vessels that are located at grade. At the all-important duty point, the pump delivers a flow of 101 m3 h-1 against a head of 20 m, and it operates with a pump efficiency of 65%. Based on these figures, the shaft power at the duty point works out at 8.5 kW, which is the power that has to be delivered to the pump shaft in order to sustain the duty. The motor that drives the pump is rated 15% above this value, which provides a certain amount of headroom above the calculated requirement at the duty point. During the acceptance test, which was run for a period of 4 h at the duty point only, no cavitation was observed at any stage, which is an encouraging sign. It is worth pointing out, however, that the test covered only the single duty point and only for that limited duration, so the results that are reported here relate specifically to that operating condition and should be interpreted in that light. The two vessels are located at grade, so the duty is stated for a transfer between vessels at the same level, and all of the figures that have been presented relate to that arrangement. Taken together, the assessment gives a clear picture of what the pump is being asked to do at its intended operating point, and of the power that has to be supplied to the shaft in order to sustain that duty on a continuous basis.
target: A centrifugal pump moving water between two vessels at grade delivers 101 m3 h-1 against a head of 20 m at the duty point, with pump efficiency 65%. Shaft power at the duty point is 8.5 kW. The motor is rated 15% above this value, so the installed rating carries a margin over the shaft power the duty requires; the margin is a rating allowance and states nothing about operation at other flows. Cavitation was not observed in the acceptance test, which ran for 4 h at the duty point only. The test result is a detection statement at one operating point: over the test at the duty flow and the duty head, no cavitation was detected. Operation away from the duty point was not tested, and longer running at the duty point was not tested either. The duty figures themselves form one consistent set at one point on the pump's range; they do not describe the pump at part load or at higher flow, where the head, the efficiency and the shaft power all take other values that are not reported here. The duty point is a single point on the operating range, chosen for the transfer between the two vessels at grade. Away from that point the pump delivers other flows against other heads, and the efficiency and the shaft power move with the operating point; the values reported here are the values at the duty point and are not a description of the pump in general. For design use, the set is read as one point with its test scope attached, and any extension of the result beyond that point requires test evidence that the acceptance run does not provide.
